brief.question: Does an explicit dimensionally regulated loop evaluation reproduce the continuum Einstein all-plus four-graviton amplitude, including its rational term?
brief.from_parent: The parent verified an angular kinetic determinant component. It did not integrate a complete loop observable. This child supplies a separate continuum reference; the finite-rank constraint problem remains open.
brief.healthy: Three box classes with multiplicity two are reconstructed from all cuts. Exact moments and independent 60-digit cube-to-simplex quadrature agree. Twelve kinematic configurations reproduce the published amplitude in magnitude and phase and pass permutation, helicity-weight and energy-scaling checks.
brief.noise: The deliberately incomplete strictly four-dimensional cut calculation has relative error one; omitting one real scalar state has relative error one-half. These are expected negative controls. This continuum calculation contains no angular N and cannot demonstrate a large-N limit.
brief.worth_a_flag: An exact formula or cut multiplicity fails; a simplex error exceeds 1e-45; a kinematic comparison exceeds 1e-10; a negative control unexpectedly agrees; or any statement calls this a finite-N Gaunt amplitude.
brief.decided: Local CPU and Python standard library only. Six independent integral cases and twelve scattering configurations with all 24 external permutations. Published scalar trees and the continuum state-count identity are declared inputs. Keep the source branch frozen after a meaningful run.
